w10_T4_011344: Sarah runs a bookstore and carefully tracks her inventory. She starts with 64 books in stock. She receives 32 books from a new distributor. That week, she decides to expand by making 9 complete sets of her collection. She adds 16 rare editions to her display. She receives a generous donation of 72 books from a nearby library. A dozen volunteers help organize the shelves. Unfortunately, 567 books are damaged during a water leak. She then prepares a 6-month supply forecast by multiplying her current inventory by 6 to account for seasonal demand. What is her 6-month supply forecast?
w10_T4_011345: A restaurant starts with 155 kilograms of rice. They order 41 more kilograms from their supplier. For an upcoming week, they multiply their supply by 3. They then multiply by 9 for a major event. They divide all rice equally among 4 banquet halls. They have also hired 20 new chefs this month. How many kilograms of rice does each hall receive?
w10_T4_011354: A teacher plans her curriculum starting with 163 minutes of core instruction. She adds 17 minutes for supplementary activities. She adds 9 minutes for reflection. She then multiplies her time by 4 to plan for four weeks of lessons. She multiplies by 8 again to plan for two months. How many hours of total instructional time does she need?
w10_T4_011356: A baker starts with 82 cups of flour. She uses half the amount for a special order, leaving her with 82/2 cups. She removes 20 cups for storage. She adds back 5 cups. She receives a shipment of 53 cups. She also receives 69 cups as a donation. She divides all her flour into 4 equal batches for different customers. Converting to pounds, how many pounds are in each batch?
w10_T4_011357: A coffee shop starts the day with 106 cups of coffee. In the morning, they add 54 more cups. At noon, they multiply their supply by 4 to prepare for the afternoon rush. As evening approaches, they multiply by 9 for the dinner service. Before closing, they multiply by 4 again for planning the next day's supply. What is their planned supply for tomorrow?
w10_T4_011358: A library starts its day with 157 books in the processing queue. They process 116 returns. They receive 53 new donations. They process another 19 returns. They remove 46 damaged books. The library director has been in charge for 25 years. How many books remain in the processing queue?
w10_T4_011368: A student starts their savings with 17 dollars. They lose 3 dollars to a friend. They earn 65 dollars from work. To plan for future spending, they multiply their amount by 4. They receive 37 dollars from their parents. They earn 65 dollars from selling textbooks. They have been saving for six months. If they convert their total to cents, how many cents do they have?
w10_T4_011374: A farmer starts with 69 sheep. He sells 17 sheep in spring. He trades 10 more sheep. He then doubles his herd through breeding. He then increases it by multiplying by 9 by acquiring nine additional herds of the same size. He purchases 15 more sheep. What is his final herd size?
w10_T4_011377: A store starts with 221 items, tracking them by individual units. In the morning, they receive 5 items. By afternoon, they have sold 150 items. By evening, they remove 31 damaged items for disposal. For weekly planning, they multiply the remaining count by 4. The district manager supervised this location for 9 years. How many items should they order for the next week?
w10_T4_011384: A factory starts with 86 units of production. They increase by a factor of 8. They then increase by a factor of 3. They divide by 3 to normalize. They add 56 more units. The factory has been operating for 40 years. What is the final production count?
w10_T4_011385: A company starts with 198 thousand dollars in revenue. They multiply by 9 to project annual revenue. They add 29 thousand from bonuses. They subtract 895 thousand in expenses. They multiply by 7 to plan for 7 years. They divide by 2 for a partnership split. They subtract 255 thousand in taxes. Converting to dollars, what is the final amount?
w10_T4_011388: Alice starts with 49 coins. She gains 32 coins. She loses 35 coins. She gains 77 coins. She loses 83 coins. Bob started with double the amount of coins that Alice did. If each coin is worth 25 cents, how many cents does Alice have?
w10_T4_011389: A bakery starts with 157 cups of flour. They multiply by 9 to prepare for large events. They add 40 more cups. They add 21 cups of whole wheat. They use 185 cups for production. They remove 284 cups for other projects. They multiply by 9 again for their next month's planning. The bakery has 15 employees. Converting to liters, what is their final flour amount?
w10_T4_011392: A student starts with 94 minutes of study time. They lose 73 minutes to distractions. They gain 12 minutes from a break. They gain 9 more minutes. They lose 21 minutes to an interruption. The library has 500 books. Converting to hours, how much study time do they have?
w10_T4_011393: A company starts with 189 employees. For a production simulation, they work with seven times their workforce. They add 73 temporary workers. They add 72 interns. They subtract 1014 positions due to changes. They hire 65 new employees. What is their final workforce size?
w10_T4_011394: Sarah and John are comparing their savings. Sarah starts with 168 dollars. She divides her savings in half. She adds 72 dollars from work. She multiplies her total by 9 for annual projections. She adds 45 dollars in interest. She multiplies by 7 to plan for 7 years. She adds 47 dollars from a bonus. John has 3000 dollars in savings. What is Sarah's 7-year savings projection?
w10_T4_011395: Lisa and Mark are comparing their book collections. Lisa starts with 78 books. She adds 24 books from a donation. She adds 30 more books. She sells 84 books at a used bookstore. She buys 75 new books. She receives 36 books as a gift. Mark has collected books for 15 years. How many books does Lisa have now?
w10_T4_011397: A warehouse tracks their inventory throughout the day. They start the day with 26 items. In the morning, they receive a shipment that is 8 times their starting amount. By afternoon, they ship out 166 items. They then divide their remaining inventory in half for evening accounting. The warehouse manager has 20 years of experience. By evening, they multiply for 8 distribution centers. For next-day planning, they multiply by 4. What is their planned inventory for tomorrow?
w10_T4_011401: A café operates throughout the day. They start with 80 customers in their database. In the morning, they lose 46 customers. By afternoon, they triple their engagement efforts, tripling the count. They gain 55 new customers. By evening, they lose 115 customers to churn. What is their final customer count?
w10_T4_011405: A store tracks sales throughout the day. They start with 116 items in stock. In the morning, they sell 76 items. By afternoon, demand increases, and they receive 4 times their remaining stock as new inventory. By evening, they divide their stock in half for accounting. They then remove 25 damaged items. The store has 12 employees working today. What is their final inventory?
w10_T4_011407: A school starts planning with 165 students. For next year, they plan to quadruple enrollment. The following year, they plan to multiply by 7. They then divide by 3 to account for attrition. They add 7 new students from a transfer program. The school building is 50 years old. What is their projected final enrollment?
w10_T4_011408: Alice and Bob are comparing their investments. Alice starts with 63 dollars. She multiplies by 4 through reinvestment. She loses 113 dollars to a downturn. She loses another 54 dollars in fees. She multiplies by 3 through a recovery. She multiplies by 6 through compound growth. Bob has invested 500 dollars. How much does Alice have after all transactions?
w10_T4_011412: A garden project begins with 181 seeds. In the morning, they plant 37 more seeds. By afternoon, they receive 64 additional seeds. By evening, they prepare for multiplication, so they multiply by 4. They then divide the total among 6 garden beds. How many seeds go in each bed?
w10_T4_011414: A factory starts with 160 units of production capacity. They divide by 5 for efficiency testing. They add 16 units from an upgrade. They multiply by 8 for next month's projection. They multiply by 4 for quarterly planning. The factory has 30 workers. What is their quarterly production projection?
w10_T4_011418: Maria and James are comparing their project budgets. Maria starts with 130 dollars. She divides by 5 for her weekly allocation. She spends 6 dollars. She multiplies by 3 for monthly planning. She adds 68 dollars in additional funding. She multiplies by 6 for annual projections. She adds 10 dollars in interest. James has budgeted 200 dollars for his project. What is Maria's annual budget projection?
